To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of K1 capsular polysaccharide can protect rough strains of E coli from serum bacteriolysis.

(1) the presence of a capsule can protect some strains of E. colli against serum bactericidal action, (2) the K1 capsule is the only one of 10 K antigens tested that can provide this protection, and (3) a strain which is rough, but expresses both K1 and other K antigens is more resistant to serum killing than one that expresses only the non-K1 capsule.

the role of the K antigens in serum resistance of E. coli.
